Searched: "The Boston Girl" narrator, first person, point of view, oral history, interview frame, and alternating narration.

Opened and reviewed the Simon & Schuster publisher excerpt, Anita Diamant’s official book page, a Boston Globe interior excerpt, Publishers Weekly reviews, Kirkus, and an explicit BookRags point-of-view description.

The Chatelaine authorized excerpt appeared in search results but returned a payment-required error when opened, so it was not used as evidence; no credible source indicated sustained second- or third-person sections.
person_note: Addie Baum is the participating first-person narrator, delivering her life story as a recorded oral monologue to her granddaughter Ava. The diagnostic Goodreads passages repeatedly expose Addie as “I” or “we,” while authorized opening and interior excerpts independently show the same voice and credible whole-book descriptions identify the oral-history structure. Direct uses of “you” address Ava, quote another speaker, or express general maxims; third-person descriptions concern people within Addie’s story and do not establish an external narrator. No credible evidence of alternating base-person sections was found.
